title: Liliha Bakery
notes: Coco puffs + Chantilly cake; the original Kuakini St spot is also a classic diner counter (other locations at Ala Moana and Waikiki).

title: Siam Garden Cafe
notes: Thai on Nimitz Hwy near Iwilei; open Mon–Fri only.

title: Hong Yeon
notes: Korean-Chinese on Isenberg St (listed as 'Hong Yun Chinese' in the family notes) — jjajangmyeon/jjamppong territory.

title: Maguro Brothers
notes: Fresh ahi don/poke counter inside Maunakea Marketplace, Chinatown (daytime, closed Sun); their Waikiki stall runs evenings.

title: YogurStory
notes: Ube pancakes; Korean-owned brunch on Keeaumoku until 3:30pm; first-come first-served (reservations only for 6+).

title: Fukurou
notes: 10-seat sushi omakase (~$100) tucked into Waikiki Shopping Plaza; dinner Tue–Fri only — book ahead.

title: Koko Head Cafe
notes: French Toast (cornflake-crusted) + breakfast bibimbap; Kaimuki brunch — expect a wait.

title: Lobster King
notes: Jja-jang-myeon / champong — Korean-Chinese seafood on S King St; the lobster jjamppong is the move.

title: Tonkatsu Kuro
notes: Katsu specialist in Ward Village (listed as 'Kuro Tonkatsu' in the family notes); opens 4pm on weekdays.

title: Han Gang
notes: 냉면 (naengmyeon) — one of the best cold-noodle bowls in town; Korean grill house on Waimanu St, Kakaako.

title: Broke Da Mouth Grindz
notes: Garlic furikake chicken + oxtail adobo (Diners Drive-ins & Dives famous); Kapolei — pairs with a Ko Olina day; very limited hours, check before going.

title: Yoshitsune
notes: Old-school traditional Japanese in the Park Shore Waikiki hotel — known for Japanese breakfast sets.

title: Shiro's Saimin Haven
notes: 65 kinds of fresh-made saimin since 1969 (listed as 'Shiro's Simon' in the family notes); Waimalu/Aiea — pairs with a Pearl Harbor day.

title: Don Quijote (Kaheka)
notes: 24-hour Japanese superstore — poke, bento, mochi, omiyage runs.

title: Da Ono Hawaiian Foods
notes: Old-school Hawaiian plates (laulau, kalua pig, poi) on Kapahulu; closed weekends; lunch-only early in the week.

title: Redfish Poke Bar by Foodland
notes: Sit-down poke bar + cocktails (listed as 'Red Fish Poke' in the family notes); the Kakaako original closed — current spot is on Ala Wai Blvd in Waikiki.

title: Island Vintage Coffee
notes: Açaí bowls + 100% Kona coffee; upstairs in Royal Hawaiian Center — busy, mostly outdoor seating.

title: Helena's Hawaiian Food
notes: James Beard 'America's Classic' since 1946 — pipikaula short ribs + kalua pig; Kalihi; open Tue–Fri only, 10am–7:30pm.

title: Tanaka of Tokyo
notes: Teppanyaki tableside show; Central location in Waikiki Shopping Plaza, dinner from 5pm (West location at Ala Moana too).

title: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck
notes: Garlic shrimp scampi plates from the graffiti truck in Kahuku (Haleiwa truck too); long lines at lunch.

title: Tsurutontan Udon
notes: House-made udon in giant bowls; Royal Hawaiian Center; takes reservations.

title: Mitch's Fish Market & Sushi Bar
notes: Tiny BYOB sushi bar by the airport runways (listed as 'Mitch's Sushi'); world-class sashimi + anything lobster; reservations essential, last seating 7:45pm.

title: 53 By The Sea
notes: Oceanfront fine dining in Kakaako with the Diamond Head view; dinner Wed–Sat + weekend brunch; reserve.

title: Yakitori Hachibei
notes: Hakata-style yakitori in Chinatown. NOTE: the original spot closed at lease-end and is reopening at Nuuanu Ave & N Hotel St — verify it's open before going.

title: Sugoi
notes: Spicy garlic chicken bento; takeout counter in City Square, Kalihi; opens 8am daily.

title: Scratch Kitchen
notes: Milk & cereal pancakes + Southern-comfort brunch; South Shore Market, Ward Village.

title: Ya-Ya's Chophouse & Seafood
notes: Kakaako steakhouse. NOTE: Yelp marks it CLOSED as of mid-2026 — verify before planning around it.

title: The Signature Prime Steak & Seafood
notes: 36th floor of the Ala Moana Hotel — sunset city views; from 4:30pm; valet or limited self-parking; reserve.

title: Il Tappo
notes: Authentic Italian oasis on Kalakaua; dinner from 5:30pm, closed Sun.

title: Ethel's Grill
notes: Kalihi hole-in-the-wall famous for tataki sashimi. NOTE: Yelp marks it CLOSED as of 2026 — verify before going.

title: Mahina & Sun's
notes: Local-sourced menu poolside at the Surfjack Hotel; live music; walk-ins from noon.

title: Nico's Pier 38
notes: Fish-auction-fresh seafood + fish-market poke on the working harbor; furikake ahi; closed Sun.

title: Takayuki
notes: Could not verify this spot on Oahu (no Yelp/press match) — confirm the exact name and location with Erica's mom's friends before booking.

title: Ono Seafood
notes: #7 Spicy Ahi — made-to-order poke by the pound on Kapahulu since 1995; closed Sun–Mon; can sell out.

title: Maguro Spot
notes: Build-your-own poke hole-in-the-wall on Kuhio Ave — best-value ahi in Waikiki; weekdays 10am–8:30pm.

title: Foodland Farms Ala Moana
notes: Supermarket poke counter — 2026 Poke Bowl champion; Ewa wing of Ala Moana Center.

title: Highway Inn
notes: Loco moco + Hawaiian plates, family-run since 1947; Kakaako location at 680 Ala Moana Blvd (SALT).

title: Ruscello at Nordstrom
notes: Quiet sit-down inside Nordstrom Ala Moana — easy mid-shopping lunch; from 11am.

title: Royal Hawaiian Bakery
notes: Malasadas (not baked daily — ask) + the famous banana bread; Pink Palace lanai, mornings only (6am–noon, weekdays).

title: Leonard's Bakery
notes: The original malasada since 1952 — order them hot; Kapahulu Ave, 5:30am–7pm daily.
